title: Cryo-EM analysis of Ebola virus nucleocapsid-like assembly
protocol: Lyse cells using an EmulsiFlex-C5 homogenizer (Avestin).
Centrifuge lysates at 30,000×g at 4°C for 40 min.
Gently transfer the supernatant to a clean container.
Filter the supernatant with a 1.2 μm filter.
Load the supernatant on a 15 ml Ni6FF column (Cytiva) equilibrated in lysis buffer.
Wash the column with 3 column volumes of lysis buffer.
Elute the bound protein with 3 column volumes of elution buffer.
Take the eluted sample and load onto a 15 ml amylose column (NEB).
Wash the column with 3 column volumes of wash buffer.
Elute the bound protein with 3 column volumes of amylose column elution buffer.
Apply eluted protein to an 8 mL Source15Q ion exchange column.
Wash the column with 3 column volumes of Source15Q ion exchange column wash buffer.
Elute the protein using a linear gradient of NaCl up to 1 M in 5 column volumes.
Add TEV protease to the target protein at a ratio of 1:100 and digest for 12–16 hours at 25°C.
Dilute the digested protein sample with wash buffer to achieve a conductivity of approximately 8 mS/cm.
Load the diluted sample onto a Source15Q ion exchange column to separate undigested protein, MBP-His6 tag, and TEV protease from the cleaved protein.
Elute the target protein using a linear gradient of NaCl up to 1 M in 5 column volumes.
Concentrate the eNP-2 protein and load onto a 120 mL 10/300 SD200 gel filtration column for final purification.
Purify with 1 column volume of storage buffer.
Collect peak 1 eluting around 52 mL from the protein purification process.
Concentrate collected eNP-2 protein using a 30 kDa ultrafiltration centrifuge tube to a final concentration of 10 mg/mL.
Determine the purity of eNP-2 assembly by Coomassie blue stained SDS-PAGE gel.
Use purified eNP-2 assembly for negative stain and cryo-EM studies immediately after purification.
Apply 2 μL of eNP-2 sample at 1 mg/mL in PBS to a glow-discharged copper grid coated with continuous carbon film.
Wait for the sample on the grid to settle for 1 minute.
Blot excess liquid from the grid using a piece of filter paper.
Apply 4 μL PBS to the grid and repeat blotting steps.
Stain with 2% uranyl acetate.
Prepare three droplets of roughly 20 μL, 20 μL, and 60 μL uranyl acetate on parafilm.
Touch the grid to the first two 20 μL droplets sequentially for 3 seconds each.
Repeat step 10 in between touching the grid to different droplets.
Wash the grid in the 60 μL droplet for 30 seconds.
Repeat step 10 after washing.
Airdry the grid before loading into the microscope.
Load the negative stained grid into the room temperature side-entry holder of JEOL JEM-1400plus Transmission Electron Microscope operating at 80 kV.
Record with an AMT XR111 high-speed CCD camera at 30,000× magnification.
Prepare liquid ethane using a foam container with liquid nitrogen as coolant and a spider-like metal piece for heat conduction.
Glow discharge Quantifoil R 1.2/1.3 Cu grids (200 mesh) for 40 seconds.
Set Mark IV Vitrobot to 4°C and 100% humidity in the chamber.
Configure Mark IV Vitrobot settings to one blot for 3 seconds, with no wait time and no drain time, zero offset.
Adjust parameters as needed based on ice thickness and distribution (e.g., increase blot time or offset if ice is too thick, increase glow discharge time if ice distribution is uneven).
Load the grids onto tweezers and lift them into the Mark IV Vitrobot chamber.
Lift liquid ethane container to the bottom of the vitrobot chamber.
Load sample from one side of the chamber onto the grid.
Blot the grid with filter papers.
Plunge the grid into liquid ethane.
Transfer the grid to the blue grid button for storage.
Load glow discharged grid onto the tweezer and place it in the chamber.
Raise the liquid ethane container to the bottom of the chamber.
Apply 2 μL of eNP-2 assembly sample to the grid from the side of the chamber.
Blot the grid for 3 seconds.
Plunge the grid into liquid ethane again.
Lower the liquid ethane container.
Load frozen grids into JEM3200FSC (JEOL) operated at 300 kV.
Set search mode magnification to 3,000× for eNP-2 helical tube visualization.
Set imaging mode magnification to 30,000× for data acquisition.
Import the raw movie frames into Relion 2.1.
Motion correct micrographs using Motioncorr v2.1 with parameters set as “Number of patches X, Y” = 5, 5 and “Iter” = 10.
Estimate contrast transfer function (CTF) using CTFFIND4 with microscope parameters and “Amount of astigmatism” = 1000.
Select micrographs with visible thon rings at better than 6 Å resolution for further analysis.
Manually select helical tubes in the selected micrographs using e2helixboxer.py in EMAN2.12 with “helix-width” set to 400.
Import txt files containing start and end point coordinates of each helical tube into Relion 2.1.
Extract segments in Relion 2.1 with parameters: Particle box size = 528, Re-scaled size = 132, Tube diameter = 500, Number of asymmetrical units (ASUs) = 5, Helical rise = 2.65.
Perform two-dimensional class averaging in Relion 2.1 with parameters: Number of classes = 200, mask diameter = 600, Limit resolution E-step = 10, Tube diameter = 500.
Select good 2D class averages and corresponding particles for further analysis.
Prepare initial model in e2initialmodel.py in EMAN2 with default parameters using selected 2D class average images as input (10 min).
Fit the model to segments of one protein monomer.
Fit the model to the cryo-EM density of one protein monomer.
Extract additional segments based on the fitted model.
Fit the model to the newly extracted cryo-EM density of one protein monomer.
Extract additional segments based on the model of the other protein monomer in the asymmetric unit.
Fit the model to the cryo-EM density of the other protein monomer in the asymmetric unit.
Rigidly fit crystal structures of several eNP-2 by alignment to corresponding segments.
Flexibly fit the rigidly fitted crystal structure to the extracted density using MDFF, moving helices a21 and a22 and the b-hairpin motif into the density.
